title: A causal map of plant-wide communication and plasmodesmatal control

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a causal explanation of how a local event in a plant produces coordinated responses elsewhere: which signals carry information, which tissues they traverse, how different routes interact, and what determines the timing and location of the response. The target is a model that can predict what changes when a particular signaling route is interrupted or restored, within explicitly tested conditions.

In the proposed framework, transport between neighboring cells through plasmodesmata is considered alongside vascular chemical signals, electrical changes and hydraulic signals. Plasmodesmatal control concerns when and where cell-to-cell passage is permitted or restricted. These mechanisms must be distinguished experimentally; the concept does not assume that every long-distance signal travels through plasmodesmata or that a single route explains every systemic response. This is the research framing supplied with the candidate, rather than a set of findings verified by the retained source.

significance.text: If achieved, this capability would turn descriptions of coordinated plant responses into explanations that support intervention. For a defined local stress, researchers could predict which distant tissues respond, when they respond, and how changing a particular route alters that outcome. Explaining coordination across tissues and timescales would be a major advance in plant physiology, especially if the same causal principles remained useful across several species.

The significance is coordination in an organism without an animal nervous system. Electrical signaling, where implicated, would not by itself establish an animal-like nervous architecture, cognition or a single central controller. The proposed account allows coordination to arise from interacting transport and signaling processes distributed across tissues.

Conditional downstream possibilities include engineering the timing or location of stress responses and using biological signaling networks for computation. Those applications would require additional evidence of controllability, specificity, reliability and acceptable effects on plant performance. A causal map alone would not establish useful crop engineering or biological computing, and success under selected stresses would not establish control over every plant response.

missing_breakthrough.text: The proposed missing capability is an experimentally grounded account connecting local signals, transport regulation and distant responses into a predictive causal model. The unresolved question is not simply whether several routes participate, but when each is necessary, when routes can compensate for one another, and how their interactions change across tissues, timescales and species. The supplied evidence does not establish how much of this capability has already been achieved.

As an experimental-design synthesis, the central barriers are observing multiple routes with sufficient spatial and temporal resolution and perturbing them selectively enough to interpret the result. A treatment that changes cell-to-cell transport may also change the condition of the treated tissue; a diminished distant response would therefore need to be distinguished from a general loss of tissue function. Similarly, signals occurring together do not establish which initiates, carries, amplifies or follows the response.

A further proposed barrier is connecting measurements across scales. A local change in plasmodesmatal passage must be related to transport through the surrounding tissue and ultimately to a measurable systemic response. A convincing model would need to explain both successful predictions and boundaries: circumstances in which a route changes role, a compensating route takes over, or a mechanism does not transfer to another species.

current_state.text: The supplied research attributes relevant background to Jacob O. Brunkard’s 2024 review, “Communicating Across Cell Walls: Structure, Evolution, and Regulation of Plasmodesmatal Transport in Plants,” with DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-62036-2_4. It describes that review as covering plasmodesmatal connections and signaling pathways that converge on transport regulation. However, the supplied review found that the retained PubMed artifact contained a cookie-access notice rather than scientific article text. The attribution and reported coverage therefore remain supplied bibliographic information, not content verified from the retained document.

The earlier statement that an abstract had been inspected must be corrected: no inspectable abstract or full review was available in the retained material. Although the source index records a saved, untruncated artifact with no extraction issues, the review reports that its 153 extracted characters were an access notice. Successful saving and extraction do not establish article identity or access to scientific content.

Consequently, this evidence package cannot substantiate specific demonstrated regulatory pathways, their experimental scope, or the present extent of a general causal account of whole-plant coordination. The artifact was retrieved on November 11, 2026, but that retrieval date does not establish scientific currency; the review also reports an empty freshness record. No quantitative performance results or dated experimental demonstrations are documented in the supplied scientific text. These limitations leave the degree of completion unresolved and do not show that the attributed biological statements are false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: apply defined local stresses in multiple species while tracking identified signaling routes and responses in specified local and distant tissues. Before intervening, use the causal model to predict the timing and location of systemic responses. Selectively perturb individual routes and relevant combinations, then test whether the resulting changes match those predictions. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, not established field standards.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed causal validation: restore an interrupted route or its relevant function and determine whether the predicted response returns at the expected time and location. Controls should establish the specificity of the intervention and distinguish disrupted communication from damaged tissue or a changed local stress response. Where several routes could compensate for one another, the demonstration should test that possibility explicitly rather than interpreting a single negative perturbation as proof that a route has no role.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed causal validation

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and boundaries: repeat the key predictions, disruptions and restorations across independent experiments, with methods sufficiently specified for independent replication. Report the tested species, tissues, developmental conditions, stresses, timescales and measurement uncertainty, alongside failed predictions. Multispecies results should distinguish shared mechanisms from species-specific behavior. Finite experiments would establish demonstrated breadth within those boundaries, not literal universality; numerical acceptance thresholds would need to be justified for the particular measurements.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility and boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: BOT-05, “Predictive plant biology from genome to whole-organism performance,” overlaps through its ambition to explain and predict behavior across biological scales. BOT-12 supplies a narrower target focused on communication routes and their causal interactions. A successful signaling model could contribute to broader organism-level prediction without completing the genome-to-performance task.

Roster-based synthesis: BOT-08, “Programmable, durable plant immunity against diverse pathogens,” and BOT-07, “Transferable resurrection-like desiccation tolerance in productive crops,” could intersect with BOT-12 when systemic communication helps coordinate responses to pathogens or water stress. Understanding those communications would not by itself establish durable immunity, survival after severe desiccation, or productive crop performance. Each remains a separate innovation with additional requirements.

Roster-based synthesis: BOT-13, “A predictive mechanism for plant cell-wall growth and mechanical sensing,” is adjacent through the relationship between cellular structure, physical signals and tissue responses. BOT-12 asks how information and transport are coordinated across cells and tissues; BOT-13 asks how wall growth and mechanical sensing work predictively. BOT-17, “Predictive control of plant cell-division planes and tissue patterning,” could intersect where intercellular communication influences development, but predicting a systemic response does not establish control of division geometry or tissue pattern.

Roster-based synthesis: BOT-16, “Predictable control of plant–mycorrhizal nutrient exchange,” could intersect with internal signaling that coordinates nutrient demand and allocation. Its central target nevertheless concerns exchange between plant and fungal partners, whereas BOT-12 concerns communication within the plant. These relationships identify potential interfaces between the roster entries without merging their identities or assuming that progress on one completes another.

change_log.reason: The review found the concept scientifically coherent; missing inspectable evidence does not justify removing or renaming it.

change_log.reason: These details clarify causal reasoning and distinguish demonstrated breadth from universal coverage without presenting proposed criteria as consensus standards.

unresolved_issues: The intended review’s identity, authorship, publication details and scientific coverage cannot be independently confirmed from the retained access notice.
The package does not provide inspectable scientific evidence for particular plasmodesmatal regulatory pathways or their roles in systemic responses.
The present degree of completion of a general causal account remains unresolved because no usable freshness evidence or scientific update was supplied.
Specific species, tissues, stresses, measurement methods, selective interventions and quantitative acceptance thresholds remain to be defined for the proposed demonstrations.
